title: Consistent Output Guarantees — PRD + Launch Slate for Hosted Generation & Retrieval Endpoints
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: PRD that defines behavioral contracts and acceptance criteria to ensure consistent outputs for hosted chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. Includes launch checklist, monitoring and rollback plans, and necessary cross-team dependencies.
background: Customers report subtle regressions and variance across model variants and fallback routes. We need a predictable contract for semantic consistency, tokenization invariants and structured output templates to avoid user-facing regressions during rollouts of model versions & routing fallbacks.
goals: Define behavioral output contracts for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Explicit acceptance criteria and tests to gate launches
Minimize regressions during model substitutions and capacity fallbacks
Operational runbook for detecting and rolling back quality regressions
non_goals: Mandating a single model for all workloads
Replacing existing eval infra; will reuse existing eval harnesses
scope_included: Chat: system/user role preservation, streaming chunk boundaries, function-call consistency
Completions: prompt-context trimming invariants, stop sequence fidelity, sampling reproducibility under same seed
Embeddings: stable vector dimensionality and cos-sim monotonicity guarantees for identical inputs
Rerank: deterministic pairwise ordering for identical scoring inputs and documented tie-break behavior
requirements: Explicit behavioral contract doc per endpoint (one-pagers) with examples and counterexamples
Automated acceptance tests runnable in CI covering 80+ realistic prompt templates
Telemetry hooks for per-tenant regression detection tied to prompt-sets
Fallback compatibility matrix that lists acceptable substitute models and their provable delta thresholds
API surface additions for clients to opt-in to 'strict-output' mode with deterministic settings
success_metrics: Launch acceptance: all acceptance tests pass in staging for three consecutive days
Production regression rate from baseline <= 0.5% for high-frequency prompt-sets in first 7 days
Time-to-detect quality regression <= 15 minutes for critical tenants
Rollback time-to-safe-state <= 30 minutes from detection to traffic cutover
acceptance_criteria: Contract docs reviewed and approved by PM, ENG, and Design
Per-endpoint automated test suites cover canonical prompt templates and edge cases
Staging: end-to-end smoke tests for stream continuity (chat) and embedding vector stability pass
QA: manual review of 100 samples per endpoint across model variants with a no-major-regression threshold
Observability: dashboards created in Console with token-level and per-prompt-set latency, error, and quality deltas
Operational: rollback playbook reviewed with on-call and SRE and runbook links embedded
launch_checklist: PRD signoff from Product, Engineering, and Design
Security review completed and sign-off from InfoSec
Release plan with staggered canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with >=24h between stages
Canary gating: automated quality gates and manual sample review at each stage
Alerting thresholds configured: quality delta, latency, error budget burn
Capacity plans validated for worst-case fallback routing
Customer communication draft for early adopters and enterprise accounts
Post-launch validation runbook and 72-hour monitoring cadence
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: model substitution creates semantic drift — Mitigation: define acceptable metric thresholds and auto-fallback
Risk: increased latency from strict-output mode — Mitigation: opt-in flag and performance budget per tenant
Risk: edge-case regressions missed by automated tests — Mitigation: curated prompt-sets from customer accounts and rolling human spot-checks
notes: We will leverage existing eval harness and example prompt-sets maintained by Applied ML. Design will provide templates for structured outputs and function-call schemas. Operations must provide token-level tracing before canary.
